0.long_answer: Parkinson's disease dementia (PDD) is the correct answer. Parkinson's disease is recognized as the second most common neurodegenerative disorder after Alzheimer's disease. In approximately 30% of cases, individuals with Parkinson's disease develop dementia. PDD is one of the two subtypes of Lewy body dementia, with the other being dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB). This means that the cognitive decline seen in Parkinson's disease dementia is part of the spectrum of Lewy body dementias, characterized by the presence of abnormal protein deposits called Lewy bodies in the brain.
